scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

Imported anambe geometry covers 1492 to 1500 in Pará, with a rough polygon larger than the recognized Anambé territory. The narrative is about Anambé people, not a nation founded in 1492 or ended in 1500. No imported geometry is certified.

ISA’s account incorporates twentieth-century reports. Descriptions of food and equipment are placed in that historical context, rather than asserting a fresh 2026 census or universal contemporary practice. Its assertion of lost Indigenous culture is not adopted.
The 1982 transfer and return are supported by ISA’s population discussion. Older numbers differ in scope and mobility, so none is presented as a definitive total population.

Lisboa’s 2020 conference paper was read for collection history, named forms and materials, and the photographic fieldwork. The conference abstract and full paper are one source for word budgeting. Museum collection dates are not archaeological occupation dates.

Some baskets were collected from use while others were made at researchers’ request. No claim is made that all objects were equally common or that a museum acquisition equals excavation. Photographs were taken into the community, not the physical collection.

The 2022 play study was downloaded and read, especially pages 10 to 13. Memories of older toys are distinguished from observed play. Publication year is not the exact date of every field observation. Broad claims that play automatically prepares every child for a gendered adult role are not repeated.

The play paper’s decree number 304 and October 1991 recognition date conflict with the original decree. The card uses Decree 380, signed December 24 and published December 26, 1991. ISA’s land database corroborates this. No legal advice or independent survey is implied.

Luakam Anambé’s museum interview transcript was read; the video and photographs were not examined. Intimate biographical details unnecessary to the craft and language account are omitted. Her planned lessons are not represented as completed training.
Funai’s separate profile is attributed as a profile of one maker. No unverified patent ownership or universal approval by all depicted peoples is asserted.
The 2021 and 2022 phases identify documented accounts, not beginnings or endings of Anambé practices. Continuity is explicit, with no artificial conquest or successor link.
Independent historical review, identity/border verification and depth certification remain pending.
